newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Shield still sees 1997 AFT sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Shield still sees 1997 AFT sales.

text.p: Shield Diagnostics Group Plc said on Friday that it still expected to see the first sales of its heart attack predictor test to go ahead this year, despite problems with a U.S.-based trial.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, technical director Peter Foster said: "We don't see it as a problem at all and we will continue with our timetable for the commercialisation of the test."

Earlier one of the doctors involved in the U.S. ARIC study, which has tracked the incidence of heart attacks in 16,000 people over more than ten years, said mishandling and storage of early blood samples may have led to "misleading conclusions."
This led to a sharp fall in Shield's share price.

Foster said the ARIC study was only one of several in progress. Shield hopes that the studies, including the ARIC study and a UK study based at St Bartholomew's hospital, London, will prove a link between a clotting agent in the blood known as Activated Factor Twelve (AFT) and propensity to heart attacks. Shield is developing a diagnostic kit which it says can show the presence of AFT in the blood.
"It is not negative news for AFT," said Foster, pointing to "good data" from the UK study of 3,000 people already published in preliminary form last month. "You are talking about sales this year."

Foster said that in the U.S. ARIC trial samples of blood were taken from the same individuals at three year intervals. The problems reported on Friday related to samples taken in 1986, which he said still left plenty of data from the U.S. trial to analyse.
"More important is the (St Bartholomew's) data which is there and getting stronger," said Foster.

He declined to comment on the view of some analysts that the company had allowed its share price, which had jumped by more than 560 percent since the start of the year to an all-time high of 928 pence earlier on Friday, to get ahead of itself.
Shares in Shield ended the day down 140 pence at 665 pence. -- Jonathan Birt London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
